_readme: BRAIN_CELL_001 -- a headless experiment (not a new component). Every part
here is an ordinary, already-validated real component from js/circuit.js
(battery, vgnd, resistor, comparator, pmos/nmos, capacitor, diffsource);
the solver has no idea this board is called 'BRAIN_CELL_001' or that any
node is called 'LEAN' or 'MEM' -- those are labels declared in
nodeNames/measurements purely for this file's own readability and for
the events/persistence checks below to refer to. Run it with:
node simulate.js experiments/brain_cell_001.json
Circuit: the same real window-comparator decision circuit validated by
test/circuit.test.js's T-WINDOW-3STATE and the Stage-1 preset in
js/app.js (presetStage1TernaryParts) -- a TLV3202 window comparator
compares a controlled LEAN signal against two resistor-divider
references (+/-~20mV around V0), and its two outputs gate a PMOS/NMOS
pair that dumps current from the P/GND rails into a sample-and-hold
node (MEM, an RC electronic hold: 100k leak + 10uF cap referenced to
V0). The only change from the validated preset is swapping the old
battery+3-switch lean selector for ONE diffsource part (lean1) -- this
is exactly the real component the milestone asked for, replacing a
multi-part selector with one controllable low-voltage source.
Stages implemented in this pass (of the user's 13-stage brain-cell
plan):
Stage 0 (reference test): s0_ref_unloaded / s0_ref_loaded /
s0_ref_recover -- V0 stays at 2.5V un-sagged under a light
real load (r5 dropped from 100k to 2k), recovers when the load
is removed.
Stage 1 (lean test): s1_lean_neg / s1_lean_zero / s1_lean_pos --
the Decision measurement (LEAN - V0) reads back the commanded
-20/0/+20mV accurately.
Stage 2 (regenerative-ish selection + write): s2_select_right --
a real +40mV lean (past the window edge) makes the comparator's
OUT1 go LOW, which is what actually switches Q1 on and dumps
real current into MEM -- the 'right_selected' event below fires
at the solver's own measured crossing time, not a scripted flag.
Stage 10 (release) + Stage 11 (new-state test): s2_release --
the lean returns to 0 (drive removed) and the circuit keeps
solving on its own; the persistence check below proves MEM stays
measurably different from its pre-selection baseline for the
entire 0.3s hold, decaying on the real 100k*10uF~=1s RC tau, not
snapping back instantly.
Explicitly NOT implemented in this pass (would need new circuit
topologies this simulator hasn't designed/validated yet, not just new
experiment JSON -- forcing them in now risked exactly the 'hidden
logical condition' failure mode the milestone explicitly warns
against): Stage 3 (first-loop oscillation test), Stage 4 (second-loop
admission), Stage 5 (coupled-loop measurement), Stage 6 (ternary
classification -- trivial to add once real Left/Hold/Right outcomes
exist, held back only because Stage 3-5 aren't built), Stage 7 (three
physical Mirror Gates), Stage 8 (six-position receipt), Stage 9 (a
real MAGNETIC-core write -- attempted here with a memorycore in place
of the RC hold, but the naive current path from the P/GND rails
through the FET pair didn't budget enough real current to cross the
core's real coercive threshold; needs a properly current-budgeted
write-driver design, not a bigger lean), Stage 12/13 (feed the result
back as the next cycle's input, recurrence).
A real solver limitation surfaced while building this (tracked
separately, not papered over): below dt~0.002s, or on a sharp
comparator decision flip, this exact circuit can numerically diverge
because the vgnd/comparator current-limit model switches to a pure
ideal current source with no bounding resistance to the supply rails
-- a real chip's output can never swing past its own supply pins, but
this model doesn't yet enforce that. All dt values here are set to
0.002s, verified clean (zero warnings) end to end. See circuit.js's
TaskList for the follow-up fix.
